rows: melting point 115 °C: A semicrystalline bar cannot hold its shape above its melting point.

45 °C floor: Heat deflection is measured by heating a loaded bar from room temperature (ISO 75, ASTM D648). A bar soft enough to deflect near room temperature has no meaningful HDT, and no filament in the snapshot measures below 48 °C even at 1.8 MPa. A soft floor, so a PE or BVOH estimate cannot reach below freezing.

Corrected 2026-09-21 (m128-specimens-the-sheet-states) against the source: the sheet states how its test bars were made, once for the table: "Testing Specimen Printing Conditions:". Flagged physically implausible 2026-10-18 (m440, D55, D149): the sheet prints a heat deflection of 90 °C at 0.455 MPa beside its own modulus of elasticity of 6~7 MPa (V005367) and an elongation at break of 400~600 %. ISO 75 records the temperature at which the loaded bar bends a further 0.2 % of outer-fibre strain; the load alone strains a 6 MPa bar about 7 %, and a 3 % fall of its modulus meets the criterion, so the bar the sheet describes cannot hold to 90 °C in that test (PBAT melts at 110 to 120 °C). The number is not a rigid bar's softening point; HDT does not apply to so soft a bar. Kept as printed; it backs nothing.

rows: Flexible filament has excellent flexibility and good fluidity.
It offers good dimensional stability, no warping, no cracking and strong layer adhesion, with the ability to be printable on various FFF 3D printers.
If issues like bubbles or severe stringing occur during printing Flexible filament, please dry the filament in a hot dry air oven at 60℃ for at least 5 hours before use.

The Flashforge product page for Flexible as the Internet Archive captured it on 2025-10-08 (the live address now answers 404). The page titles the product "Flashforge PLA Flexible Filament" where the registered TDS says PBAT; it is taken as the same product (same name, shop address and SKU). Its windows differ from the TDS's (nozzle 190~240 vs 200~240 C, bed 25~60 vs room temperature~60 C, speed 20~200 vs 30~150 mm/s) and its drying schedule is 70 C for 5 hours where the TDS says 60 C for at least 5 hours: both statements stand.
